metadata.name: PlaceRate
metadata.reference: Based on Creating Vibrant Communities by Dean Landy

elements.name: Transport
elements.description: Connectivity to public and active transport networks
elements.communityDescription: How easy is it to get to and from this place without a car?

questions.q: Does the project have direct access to public transport?
questions.communityQ: Can you easily catch a bus, train or tram here?
questions.communityWhy: Good transport links mean less traffic, cleaner air, and a more connected community.

questions.q: How close is the nearest train/tram/bus stop?
questions.communityQ: How close is the nearest public transport stop?
questions.communityWhy: Being able to walk to a stop makes a huge difference to daily life — especially for people without cars.

questions.q: Which active transport options are available?
questions.communityQ: Which of these are available for getting around?
questions.communityWhy: Walking and cycling options make a place healthier, safer, and more affordable to live in.

elements.improvement: Add dedicated cycling infrastructure and improve pedestrian connectivity.

elements.name: Public realm
elements.description: Publicly accessible spaces the community can use and interact within
elements.communityDescription: Are there good public spaces where people can gather, relax, and connect?

questions.q: Does the project have a central place for gathering?
questions.communityQ: Is there a central public space — like a square or plaza — where the community can gather?
questions.communityWhy: Public gathering spaces are the heart of a community. They encourage social connection and community events.

questions.q: Are there areas where pedestrians are prioritised?
questions.communityQ: Are paths and streets designed for people first, not just cars?
questions.communityWhy: Pedestrian-friendly streets make communities safer, more walkable, and more enjoyable.

questions.q: Which public realm features are included?
questions.communityQ: Which of these outdoor features are included?
questions.communityWhy: Parks, gardens, and markets create places people want to spend time in.

elements.improvement: Create more pedestrian-priority zones and gathering spaces.

elements.name: Retail & food
elements.description: Retail, dining, and daily needs within the precinct
elements.communityDescription: Are there good shops, cafes, and daily services nearby?

questions.q: Does the project include ground-floor retail activation?
questions.communityQ: Are there shops, cafes, or services at street level that bring life to the area?
questions.communityWhy: Active street frontages make places feel safe and vibrant — there are always people around.

questions.q: How close is the nearest supermarket?
questions.communityQ: How close is the nearest supermarket or fresh food store?
questions.communityWhy: Access to fresh food is essential for community health and convenience.

questions.q: What food & beverage types are planned?
questions.communityQ: What kinds of food and drink options are available or planned?
questions.communityWhy: A variety of food choices means everyone in the community — different budgets, tastes, and dietary needs — is catered for.

elements.improvement: Increase activated ground-floor uses and food & beverage diversity.

elements.name: Education
elements.description: Education providers and learning opportunities nearby
elements.communityDescription: Are there good educational facilities and childcare options nearby?

questions.q: Is there a community space for other education providers?
questions.communityQ: Is there a community space for learning — like a library, hall, or education centre?
questions.communityWhy: Access to learning spaces benefits people of all ages, from young children to seniors.

questions.q: Where is the nearest childcare?
questions.communityQ: How close is the nearest childcare centre?
questions.communityWhy: Accessible childcare is essential for families, especially parents returning to work.

questions.q: Which education types are accessible?
questions.communityQ: Which of these learning options are available nearby?
questions.communityWhy: A mix of education options supports the whole community — from babies to adults.

elements.improvement: Ensure childcare and library access within walking distance.

elements.name: Health & wellbeing
elements.description: Access to health services and wellness facilities
elements.communityDescription: How easy is it to access health services and stay active?

questions.q: Is there a GP or medical centre within the precinct?
questions.communityQ: Is there a doctor, medical centre, or health clinic in or near this project?
questions.communityWhy: Nearby healthcare means quicker access in an emergency and better long-term health outcomes for residents.

questions.q: How close is the nearest hospital?
questions.communityQ: How close is the nearest hospital?
questions.communityWhy: Even if you hope to never need it, hospital proximity matters for families, elderly residents, and people with health needs.

questions.q: Which health facilities are on-site or nearby?
questions.communityQ: Which health and wellbeing services are available?
questions.communityWhy: A full range of health services keeps people healthy and reduces pressure on hospitals.

elements.improvement: Include on-site allied health and fitness facilities.

elements.name: Sustainable
elements.description: Renewable energy and sustainable design features
elements.communityDescription: Is this project designed with the environment in mind?

questions.q: Are you looking to use or create renewable energy sources?
questions.communityQ: Does this project use renewable energy like solar panels?
questions.communityWhy: Renewable energy lowers electricity bills for residents and reduces the project's impact on the environment.

questions.q: Which sustainable energy types are planned?
questions.communityQ: Which types of renewable or clean energy are included?
questions.communityWhy: The more clean energy sources a project uses, the more resilient and environmentally friendly it is.

questions.q: Are water reuse or recycling systems included?
questions.communityQ: Does the project recycle or reuse water?
questions.communityWhy: Water recycling reduces pressure on the water network and helps the community be more resilient during droughts.

elements.improvement: Incorporate solar systems and water recycling programs.

elements.name: Housing diversity
elements.description: Range of dwelling types and affordability
elements.communityDescription: Does this project offer a variety of homes for different people and budgets?

questions.q: Does the project include diverse housing types?
questions.communityQ: Does the project include different types of homes — not just one kind of apartment or house?
questions.communityWhy: A mix of housing types means people at different life stages and budgets can all find a place to live.

questions.q: Is affordable or social housing included?
questions.communityQ: Does the project include affordable or social housing?
questions.communityWhy: Affordable housing is essential for teachers, nurses, retail workers, and others who keep communities running.

questions.q: Which housing types are planned?
questions.communityQ: Which types of homes are included or planned?
questions.communityWhy: Greater variety means more people can find a home that works for them.

elements.improvement: Introduce affordable housing and increase dwelling type diversity.

elements.name: Economy & employment
elements.description: Local employment, commercial, and economic activation
elements.communityDescription: Does the project create local jobs and economic activity?

questions.q: Does the project include commercial or office space?
questions.communityQ: Does the project include offices, shops, or other spaces where people can work?
questions.communityWhy: Local employment opportunities mean shorter commutes, stronger local spending, and a more self-sufficient community.

questions.q: Are there co-working or incubator spaces planned?
questions.communityQ: Are there co-working spaces, studios, or incubators for small businesses and start-ups?
questions.communityWhy: Spaces for small businesses and entrepreneurs help create a diverse, innovative local economy.

questions.q: Which economic uses are included?
questions.communityQ: Which types of economic activity are planned?
questions.communityWhy: A mix of economic uses makes a place more resilient — if one sector struggles, others keep the community going.

elements.improvement: Add co-working spaces and incubator facilities.

elements.name: Infrastructure
elements.communityDescription: Does this project have the infrastructure to support modern life?

questions.q: Does the project include high-speed digital connectivity?
questions.communityQ: Is high-speed internet (NBN or fibre) available in this project?
questions.communityWhy: Fast internet is now as essential as electricity — for working from home, education, and staying connected.

questions.q: Are smart city or digital infrastructure elements planned?
questions.communityQ: Are there smart or future-ready features like EV charging or smart lighting?
questions.communityWhy: Future-ready infrastructure saves money in the long run and helps residents transition to cleaner technology.

questions.q: Which infrastructure types are included?
questions.communityQ: Which of these infrastructure features are included?
questions.communityWhy: Good infrastructure supports daily life and makes a community more sustainable and connected.

elements.improvement: Ensure fibre connectivity and EV charging provision.

elements.name: Vision & identity
elements.description: Clear project vision and sense of place identity
elements.communityDescription: Does this place have a clear identity — something that makes it unique and special?

questions.q: Does the project have a clear and documented community vision?
questions.communityQ: Does this project have a clear vision for what kind of community it wants to be?
questions.communityWhy: Places with a strong vision tend to develop a stronger sense of community over time.

questions.q: Is there a unique identity or branding for the place?
questions.communityQ: Is there something distinctive about the design or character of this place?
questions.communityWhy: Distinctive places are more memorable, more valued, and create stronger community pride.

questions.q: Which identity elements are included?
questions.communityQ: Which of these identity features are part of the project?
questions.communityWhy: Art, heritage, and landscape character all contribute to a place that people feel genuinely connected to.

elements.improvement: Develop a clear place identity and commission public art.

elements.name: People & inclusion
elements.communityDescription: Is this project designed so everyone feels welcome — regardless of age, ability, or background?

questions.q: Is the project designed to be accessible for all ages and abilities?
questions.communityQ: Is this project designed to be accessible for people of all ages and abilities?
questions.communityWhy: Universal design benefits everyone — parents with prams, elderly residents, people with disabilities, and delivery workers.

questions.q: Are community consultation processes in place?
questions.communityQ: Have community members been consulted during the design process?
questions.communityWhy: When communities are involved in design, the outcome better reflects what people actually need.

questions.q: Which inclusion strategies are included?
questions.communityQ: Which of these inclusion features are part of the project?
questions.communityWhy: The more inclusive a community is, the stronger and more resilient it becomes.

elements.improvement: Strengthen inclusive design and community consultation.

elements.name: Safety & security
elements.description: Safe environments through design and management
elements.communityDescription: Does this place feel safe — day and night?

questions.q: Has CPTED been applied to the design?
questions.communityQ: Has the design been set up to reduce crime and make people feel safe — for example through good lighting and clear sightlines?
questions.communityWhy: Good design can make a huge difference to how safe people feel — and actually be.

questions.q: Are 24/7 activated edges or passive surveillance elements included?
questions.communityQ: Are there active frontages and people around at most times of the day?
questions.communityWhy: Places with people around naturally feel safer. "Eyes on the street" deters crime without needing security guards.

questions.q: Which safety elements are included?
questions.communityQ: Which of these safety features are included?
questions.communityWhy: A combination of safety features works better than any single measure alone.

elements.improvement: Apply CPTED principles and improve passive surveillance.

elements.name: Events & activation
elements.description: Programming, events, and ongoing place activation
elements.communityDescription: Will this place have regular events, activities, and things to do?

questions.q: Is there a plan for regular events and programming?
questions.communityQ: Is there a plan for regular community events, markets, or activities in this place?
questions.communityWhy: Regular programming brings people together, supports local businesses, and makes a place feel alive.

questions.q: Are temporary or pop-up activation spaces planned?
questions.communityQ: Are there flexible spaces that can be used for pop-up events, markets, or community activities?
questions.communityWhy: Flexible spaces mean the community can adapt the place to their needs as they evolve.

questions.q: Which activation types are intended?
questions.communityQ: What kinds of events and activities are planned?
questions.communityWhy: A variety of events means there's something for everyone — families, young people, seniors, and everyone in between.

elements.improvement: Establish a programming calendar and flexible event spaces.

elements.name: Nature & biophilia
elements.description: Connection to nature and biodiversity within the precinct
elements.communityDescription: Is nature woven into this project — trees, gardens, wildlife?

questions.q: Is there meaningful tree canopy cover planned?
questions.communityQ: Is there meaningful tree cover — not just a few token plants?
questions.communityWhy: Tree canopy provides shade, reduces urban heat, improves air quality, and makes streets more pleasant.

questions.q: Are biodiversity or habitat features included?
questions.communityQ: Are there features that support local wildlife and biodiversity?
questions.communityWhy: Biodiversity features like wetlands and wildlife corridors help maintain a healthy local ecosystem.

questions.q: Which nature elements are included?
questions.communityQ: Which of these nature features are included?
questions.communityWhy: Every green feature adds up — together they create a healthier, cooler, and more beautiful community.

elements.improvement: Increase tree canopy and introduce biodiversity corridors.

elements.name: Arts & culture
elements.description: Cultural programming, creative spaces, and public art
elements.communityDescription: Does this project celebrate creativity and culture?

questions.q: Does the project include dedicated arts or creative spaces?
questions.communityQ: Are there dedicated spaces for art, creativity, or cultural activities?
questions.communityWhy: Creative spaces support local artists, attract visitors, and give a community a distinctive cultural identity.

questions.q: Is public art commissioned or planned?
questions.communityQ: Is public art part of the design?
questions.communityWhy: Public art makes places more beautiful, reflects community identity, and gives people something to be proud of.

questions.q: Which arts elements are included?
questions.communityQ: Which arts and cultural features are included?
questions.communityWhy: Arts and culture bring people together and contribute to a community's long-term vibrancy.

elements.improvement: Commission public art and create dedicated creative spaces.

elements.name: Play & recreation
elements.communityDescription: Are there good places to play, exercise, and have fun?

questions.q: Are dedicated play spaces included for children?
questions.communityQ: Are there dedicated play spaces for children?
questions.communityWhy: Good play spaces are essential for children's development, and they give families a reason to spend time outside.

questions.q: Are sporting or fitness facilities included?
questions.communityQ: Are there places to play sport or exercise?
questions.communityWhy: Access to sport and fitness facilities improves physical and mental health across the whole community.

questions.q: Which recreation types are included?
questions.communityQ: Which recreation options are available or planned?
questions.communityWhy: A variety of recreation options means everyone — from toddlers to seniors — has somewhere to be active.

elements.improvement: Add play areas and informal recreation spaces for all ages.

elements.name: Governance
elements.description: Long-term community management and ownership models
elements.communityDescription: Will residents have a say in how this place is managed over time?

questions.q: Is there a community management or body corporate structure planned?
questions.communityQ: Is there a plan for how this community will be managed and governed over time?
questions.communityWhy: Good governance means problems get solved, maintenance happens, and the community's voice is heard.

questions.q: Are there mechanisms for ongoing community input?
questions.communityQ: Will there be regular opportunities for residents to provide feedback and shape decisions?
questions.communityWhy: Communities where residents have ongoing input tend to be happier, better maintained, and more cohesive.

questions.q: Which governance models are planned?
questions.communityQ: Which of these governance approaches are planned?
questions.communityWhy: The right governance model depends on the community — but having one is essential.

elements.improvement: Establish a community management body and resident voice.

elements.name: Aging in place
elements.description: Design features supporting residents across the life course
elements.communityDescription: Is this place designed to support people at every stage of life — including as they get older?

questions.q: Is the project designed to support aging in place?
questions.communityQ: Is this project designed so that people can comfortably live there as they age?
questions.communityWhy: 'Aging in place' means people don't have to leave their community as they get older — maintaining connections and independence.

questions.q: Are intergenerational uses planned?
questions.communityQ: Are there activities or spaces that bring different generations together?
questions.communityWhy: Intergenerational connections benefit everyone — young people gain wisdom, older people stay connected and active.

questions.q: Which aging-friendly features are included?
questions.communityQ: Which aging-friendly features are included?
questions.communityWhy: Small design choices — like rest points and accessible paths — make a huge difference to older residents and people with mobility challenges.

elements.improvement: Improve universal access and create intergenerational programming.
